classifications.rationale: FocusTrace reports repeated valid single-code-point accesskey tokens case-insensitively across the document and scopes component findings without losing document-wide collision context. Browser/platform shortcut assignment and malformed token handling remain outside the bounded warning, so the relationship is partial.

FocusTrace now enforces a bounded set of normative ARIA in HTML host-role constraints for high-impact native elements and keeps the rule findings-only. It does not yet synchronize the complete condition-dependent ARIA in HTML host-element matrix, so the benchmark relationship is partial.
standards: ARIA in HTML document conformance requirements

classifications.rationale: FocusTrace now checks exposed dialog and alertdialog semantics, including native dialog markup, for a usable accessible name and reports missing names as ARIA authoring warnings; its local AccName implementation remains deliberately bounded.
FocusTrace does not currently check role=text for focusable descendants.

FocusTrace now checks exposed treeitem roles for a usable accessible name and excludes descendant group subtrees from name-from-content evidence, while retaining warning semantics and a bounded local AccName implementation.

FocusTrace now reviews exposed native and ARIA headings that have no usable text or alternative naming contribution. The local content heuristic is deliberately bounded, so this remains partial rather than exact benchmark equivalence.

FocusTrace reports exposed native and supported ARIA table header cells without usable header text as an authoring warning. Hidden table roots are excluded and outcome semantics deliberately differ from the benchmark, so this is overlap rather than equivalent.

This rule verifies whether axe-core itself was injected into nested frames. FocusTrace uses its own local inspection architecture, so requiring the axe-core script would contradict the benchmark-only constraint.
FocusTrace reports skipped heading levels for REVIEW, covering the principal static ordering signal without claiming axe's full semantic ordering behavior.
FocusTrace validates whether images have an accessible name or are decorative, but it does not compare alt text with adjacent visible text for redundancy.

FocusTrace now explicitly reviews exposed native and supported ARIA form controls whose accessible name comes only from title, while its existing placeholder-derived naming review covers another persistent-label risk. Broader hidden-label and platform-specific authoring edge cases remain outside the bounded detector.

FocusTrace now reviews exposed banner landmarks nested inside another landmark within the same document/application scope. It retains APG-guidance REVIEW semantics rather than reproducing axe best-practice failure behavior.
FocusTrace now reviews exposed contentinfo landmarks nested inside another landmark within the same document/application scope. It retains APG-guidance REVIEW semantics.

FocusTrace validates invalid native main hierarchy and now also reviews nested explicit main landmarks. The combined evidence overlaps the benchmark while preserving separate HTML-authoring and APG-guidance outcomes.
